summary: Part 2 of the "10.0 Quality guidelines (Seller & KAMs)" video (03:57 to 05:25) walks through the banned-elements list (grading, wrong item, parts, locks and IMEI), the phone and laptop grade and functional rules, accepted physical damage, and the most common rejection reasons, then ends on a recap slide. All 17 frames listed in the pack (t00237 to t00324) were opened. The trainer only pages through slides, so there are no software steps, and the rules, thresholds and percentages come from the on-screen slides. Nothing in the frames is out of date or contains personal data. The accepted physical damage frame (t00310) has no legible rule text, and the rejection-reason chart may be cut off, so those are listed as unclear. The slide and narration disagree on who checks banned-element claims (Revibe team vs KM), which is also listed as unclear.

unclear.issue: The slide says 'Revibe team to check these claims one by one' (t00237.jpg), but the narration says 'You, as a KM then check these claims one by one.' Who checks the claims cannot be settled from the evidence, so the fact uses the slide wording and is marked medium confidence.

Narration says 'It still holds a previous customer's data'; the slide (t00280.jpg) says 'Device not factory reset - previous user data still present'. The slide wording is used in the facts.

The trainer says 'Below that, you'll find examples of the physical damage we accept' but the accepted-damage frame (t00310.jpg) shows only a laptop photo with the caption 'Accepted physical damage' and no legible rule text. The specific damage examples cannot be stated from the evidence.

The rejection-reason percentages (Battery level 32%, Physical condition 30%, Camera dot 11%, Display issue 7%, Face ID failure 5%, Speaker issue 2%) have no visible date, period or base. It is unclear what they are a percentage of, and the trainer's claim that these reasons 'drive most claims' is not quantified on screen.
The chart on t00312.jpg is cut off at the bottom edge after 'Speaker issue 2%'. Whether more rejection reasons follow below it cannot be confirmed from the frame.
